tasks.title: Implement Strom adapter command application
tasks.description: Translate open-weave desired definitions into Strom flow create/update/start/stop calls via weave-adapter-strom. README now documents this as future controller work; current adapter only observes /api/flows and reports endpoints.
notes: Implemented via the desired-hop loop: adapter pulls GET /nodes/{id}/desired, diffs against Strom /api/flows by hop id, creates/starts/deletes weave-owned flows, reports HopStatus in heartbeats. Controller provisions only through PUT /nodes/{id}/desired and no longer links weave-strom. Spec-change re-provisioning is tracked separately.

tasks.title: Edited streams are not re-provisioned (adopt-by-name has no spec-drift detection)
tasks.description: The adapter diffs desired hops against Strom flows by hop id only; if a stream definition changes but its hop ids stay the same, the existing flows are adopted unchanged and the edit never reaches the node. Add a spec hash to the hop id or a desired_hash the adapter compares so spec changes trigger re-provisioning.
notes: diff_hops now detects drift: an adopted flow whose srt:// element URIs differ from the desired hop (host or port) is deleted+recreated instead of adopted, preserving delete-before-create ordering. A flow with no parseable URI is still adopted (conservative). parse_srt_endpoint helper added to weave-strom. Landed with the collision-aware allocator (t_20260714000001_prtcol).

tasks.title: Fan-out streams only provision the first destination
tasks.description: Controller path derivation builds a hop chain for the first destination only; any additional destinations in a StreamDefinition are silently dropped. Observed on the bench fanout manifest: node-1 gets one sender hop, node-2 one receiver hop, and no hop is placed for the second destination. Expected: every entry in destinations[] is provisioned.
notes: Fixed in 611e949 (+bench support 6f3b03a, README 16b9c29): DesiredHop.egresses is now a Vec; derive_path emits one tee-based sender hop with N egresses plus one receiver hop per destination (weave-{stream}-receiver-{i}), all-or-nothing placement. Verified on the real bench: fanout with producer + both consumers reached flowing on BOTH destinations (receiver-0 on node-2, receiver-1 co-located on node-1); detaching one consumer degraded the stream and reattaching restored flowing; basic regression still flowing with the unchanged linear flow shape. Sender per-branch stats gap tracked as t_20260709130500_tq4m2n.

tasks.title: Bench producer/consumer are hardwired to the basic manifest addresses
tasks.description: The bench producer pushes to strom-1:7001 and the consumer pulls from strom-2:7003, matching only the basic scenario. As a result reverse (source listener on node-2) and same-node (receiver output on node-1) cannot be driven to flowing by the bundled verification endpoints. Make the verification endpoints parameterizable per scenario so every manifest can be exercised end to end.
notes: Fixed in 388ae48: producer-up/consumer-up take an optional host:port (defaults = prior basic addresses) passed via PRODUCER_TARGET/CONSUMER_SOURCE compose env vars; route sidecars now install both node-subnet routes. Verified on the real bench: basic (defaults), reverse (producer 172.27.0.10:7001, consumer 172.26.0.10:7003), and same-node (consumer 172.26.0.10:7003) each reached flowing.

tasks.title: Re-applying a manifest on the same ports stays pending ~10-15s after removing the prior stream
tasks.description: Applying a manifest immediately after stream-rm on the same SRT ports leaves the new stream pending for ~10-15s while the prior flow's socket release lags the delete. Reconciliation should free the ports and converge promptly once the prior definition is deleted rather than requiring a wait between apply cycles.
notes: Fixed in 772a5a8: adapter reconcile now runs delete->create->start (was create-first, so the new flow's start raced the old flow still holding the listener port and burned a full poll cycle as a spurious failed status). Added FlowApi trait + recording-fake regression test asserting deletes precede creates. Bench before/after on rm->re-apply same ports: baseline awaiting_input at ~12.0/12.0/16.9s with a failed detour at ~7s; after fix ~7.6/7.0/7.0s with no failures. Remaining ~7s is the 5s controller tick + 5s adapter poll cadence floor, not a defect. Strom-side socket release measured sub-second (delete 07:25:23.007 -> provisioned 07:25:23.534 same cycle), so no external residual and no in-cycle retry needed.

tasks.title: Sender hop reports only the first tee branch's egress stats for fan-out
tasks.description: A fan-out sender flow is srtsrc->tee->N x srtsink, but FlowStats::egress() (crates/strom/src/stats.rs:35) returns only the first srtsink, so the sender HopStatus egress condition and LinkStats.egress_rate_mbps reflect branch 0 only; other branches' per-sink rate/connection are invisible and loss counters are summed across callers without per-branch attribution. Status rollup is unaffected because each receiver hop carries its destination's health (verified on the bench fanout manifest: detaching either consumer degrades the stream), so this is an observability gap, not a correctness bug. Expose per-branch/per-destination sender egress stats (e.g. a Vec keyed by srtsink index or destination).
tasks.source: crates/strom/src/stats.rs (FlowStats::egress first-sink only); crates/adapter-strom/src/main.rs hop_statuses; follow-up from t_20260709122940_pvug8q fan-out fix

tasks.title: Adapter cannot detect EOS-dead Strom flows (Strom reports running:true/Playing after EOS)
tasks.description: Observed live during the srtsrc keep-listening incident: a flow whose srtsrc hit an SRT socket error EOSed and stopped serving, but Strom /api/flows kept reporting running:true and gst_state Playing, so HopStatus showed the hop healthy while the listener port was dead. keep-listening:true (95d2dce) removes the common idle-death trigger, but any future EOS would still be invisible to weave. Strom state reporting is external; on our side the adapter could infer death from srt-stats staleness or socket probes.
tasks.source: strom-1 logs 2026-07-10 07:36 (Error on SRT socket srtsrc_0 -> reached end of stream, flow still running:true/Playing); follow-up from keep-listening fix 95d2dce
notes: Fixed report-only in b348e03/ac5521f/adf13b1/661b35d: adapter tracks per-hop bytes_received progress across polls (ever_flowed gate, gst_state=Paused filtered, 3-poll threshold); frozen progress emits LinkCondition::Stalled and roll_up_path maps stalled hops to degraded. Verified on the bench via fault injection (weave-basic-sender recreated with keep-listening=false through the adopt-by-name path, killed by producer disconnect): ingress stalled at t+16s, stream degraded at t+20s; fresh never-fed stream stayed awaiting_input 40s without false positive; healthy disconnect/reconnect recovered to flowing in ~8s. Gotcha baked into tests: SRT settles bytes_received DOWNWARD at caller disconnect, so decreases count as no-progress, not flow reset. Remediation deliberately excluded: polling cannot distinguish dead from intentionally quiet, tracked as t_20260710093000_rmed8q.

tasks.title: Consider auto-remediating stalled weave flows (delete+recreate)
tasks.description: Stall detection (t_20260710081500_kls3nr) is report-only by design: polled surfaces cannot distinguish an EOS-dead flow from an intentionally quiet one, and keep-listening=true flows recover on their own when the caller returns, so blind restart risks thrashing healthy quiet listeners. If remediation is wanted, gate delete+recreate on a much longer confirmation window plus cooldown, or find a positive death signal (e.g. SRT handshake probe against the listener port).
tasks.source: deferred from t_20260710081500_kls3nr stall-detection design (live-bench research 2026-07-10)

tasks.title: External peers cannot discover controller-assigned ports for node-referenced endpoints
tasks.description: Node-referenced addressing assigns the receiver's listen port (and consumer egress port = listen+1) deterministically from the node's declared range, so no manifest IP/port is needed for internal sender->receiver wiring. But external producers/consumers still need a concrete host:port and there is no surface exposing the assigned ports. The bench therefore keeps raw-url pins (srt://IP:PORT + node) so producer/consumer ports stay predictable; the clean node-ref path (examples/*.yaml) is exercised only by unit tests, not end to end. Expose assigned ports (controller /status per hop, or a resolved-endpoint API) so external peers can attach, or let a destination pin only the externally-facing egress port.
tasks.source: crates/controller/src/path.rs (port_in_range / resolve_delivery); bench keeps raw pins; node-ref output addressing work

tasks.title: Unknown data-plane alias is rejected at placement, not as a northbound 4xx at apply time
tasks.description: The node-ref design called for an unknown alias to surface as a clear 4xx at apply time, but the northbound has no node registry (nodes live in the southbound), so it cannot validate aliases when a stream is submitted. Currently an unknown alias / missing default / absent port range surfaces at controller placement (derive_path -> PlacementError::UnknownAlias|NoPortRange) and the stream stays pending with a warn log, rather than being rejected on apply. To get apply-time rejection, give the northbound read access to registered node capabilities (e.g. query southbound /nodes) and validate node+alias before accepting.
tasks.source: crates/northbound/src/main.rs (no node registry); crates/controller/src/path.rs derive_path UnknownAlias; node-ref output addressing work

tasks.title: Collision-aware port assignment in controller
tasks.description: Ports are assigned by FNV-hashing the hop id into the node's shared port_range; sender ingress, receiver ingress, and consumer (dest_port + 1) ports can collide across streams on the same node, and dest_port + 1 can land outside the declared range. Now that url pinning is removed, every stream depends on assignment. Controller sees all hops per node per tick, so make assignment collision-aware there.
notes: Added a per-tick collision-aware PortAllocator in controller path.rs: per-node occupancy set, FNV preferred offset then forward linear probe (wrapping within range), PortRangeExhausted -> Pending. derive_path takes &mut PortAllocator; reconcile_once builds one per tick and iterates streams sorted by name. Consumer port is now a first-class claim (no dest_port+1). Landed with the adapter drift-recreate fix (t_20260709125000_sp7h4x).

tasks.title: resolved_ingress ignores data-plane alias (always default host)
tasks.description: The adapter reports listener addresses using only the default alias host (provision.rs resolved_addr), and connect_target prefers the reported address; a network: wan delivery can be rewritten to the default host after the receiver reports. Carry the advertised alias host in the receiver's SocketSpec.host or in HopStatus.
notes: Root-caused: dropped the resolved_ingress override from egress targeting (removed connect_target/is_wildcard_host); sender egress now unconditionally uses the alias-resolved planned delivery (host + controller-assigned port). resolved_ingress kept for observability. Regression test asserts a wan destination keeps its wan host even when a concrete resolved_ingress reports the default host.

tasks.title: Bench adapter public_endpoint points at Strom port, not adapter control API
tasks.description: bench/config/adapter-*.yaml set public_endpoint to http://172.2x.0.10:8080 (Strom's port) matching the old compose env, but the adapter control API listens on :8091. Harmless today since nothing dials the registered endpoint, but a latent mislabel.

tasks.title: Unify media-node and adapter node-config file shapes
tasks.description: media-node loads a bare NodeConfig while the adapter wraps it under a node: key (plus strom: section). Pick one shape (probably the wrapped form) so node config files are interchangeable.

tasks.title: Support remote: on stream source (pull from external listener)
tasks.description: remote: destinations shipped (sender dials out to an external SRT listener; no receiver hop, no port assignment). The source side still rejects remote (PlacementError::RemoteSource + northbound 400). Supporting a remote source needs a 'which local node hosts the caller/puller' concept so the controller can place a hop that dials the external listener and re-serves the stream internally.

tasks.title: Route sidecar routes are lost when a bench service container is restarted
tasks.description: docker compose restart <svc> recreates the container netns, dropping routes installed by its route-* sidecar (restart: "no"). After restarting southbound during persistence verification, adapters could not reach it until route-southbound was re-run manually. Make route sidecars restart: unless-stopped or re-assert routes automatically.
tasks.source: bench/docker-compose.yml; observed during persistence-layer bench verification (commit 211efb5)
notes: Also bites adapter recovery testing: docker compose stop/start adapter-1 loses routes the same way, so node-recovery verification needs a manual --force-recreate route-adapter-1. Consider a just recipe that restarts an adapter together with its route sidecar. Observed during heartbeat-TTL bench verification.
